clue.text: College beginning to provide for growth

parts.note: a poly is short for a polytechnic, a kind of college

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of provide is taken

explanation.surface: A college starting to make provision for its expansion.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyp is a small abnormal growth on a mucous membrane, such as in the nose.

clue.text: Priest warning about insects bluebottles

indicators.note: about means going round, so the warning word wraps the insects

parts.note: an omen is a warning sign
lice are small parasitic insects

explanation.surface: A clergyman cautions people about insects, namely blowflies.
explanation.walkthrough: Bluebottles looks like more insects after 'insects', but it is old slang for police officers, from their blue uniforms.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluebottle is dated British slang for a police officer, named for the blue uniform.

clue.text: Yellow being worn — the European (a Frenchman) is leading

indicators.note: leading means coming in front, so the Frenchman goes ahead of the worn piece

parts.note: le is 'the' in French, a European language
M is short for Monsieur, a Frenchman's title
clothes being worn are on

explanation.surface: Something yellow is worn, and a Frenchman takes the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon is a pale yellow colour, named after the citrus fruit.

clue.text: Government reshuffles — I cop it all!

indicators.note: a cabinet reshuffle rearranges ministers, so these letters are rearranged too

explanation.surface: A politician exclaims about a cabinet reshuffle that they will take all the blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Political matters are those relating to government and the state.

clue.text: He's the cop concealed in the bottom drawer

indicators.note: concealed means disguised, so the letters of this phrase are disguised by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A policeman is hiding in the bottom drawer of a chest.
explanation.walkthrough: A bottom drawer (British) is where a woman once collected linen and household goods for her marriage; in America that is a hope chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A hope chest is the American name for a chest of linen kept against marriage, the British bottom drawer.

clue.text: Why Haig devised a direct course of action

indicators.note: devised means worked out or contrived, so these letters are contrived into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about why Field Marshal Haig planned a straightforward military course.
explanation.walkthrough: Haig was the British commander on the Western Front in the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: A highway, figuratively, is a direct route or straightforward way to some goal.

clue.text: Chauvinist group kept in touch

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so the group sits within the touch

parts.note: a pat is a light touch
a trio is a group of three

explanation.surface: A jingoistic group stayed in contact.
explanation.definitionFit: Chauvinism originally meant excessive nationalism, so a chauvinist is an extreme nationalist.

clue.text: Wood provided by 1dn, they say

indicators.note: they say signals that the word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: the answer to 1 Down means police officers, informally cops

explanation.surface: A wood supplied by the police, as the saying goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small wood or thicket of trees.

clue.text: Article I tailored badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters come out jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to poor tailoring of an item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests clothing beside 'tailored'; it is a newspaper article.
explanation.definitionFit: An editorial is a newspaper article giving the editor's opinion, a leader.

clue.text: Captured army on the range

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the army comes first

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
ken is the range of one's knowledge or sight

explanation.surface: An army captured on the firing range.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken is the past participle of take, meaning seized or captured.

clue.text: Meat, we hear, accompanied by pickle produced from a bulb

indicators.note: we hear signals a word heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: lamb is meat from a young sheep
a pickle is a predicament, a plight

explanation.surface: Meat served with pickle, and something produced from an onion bulb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' suggests a vegetable beside the food; it is a light bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamplight is light given off by a lamp, whose source is an electric bulb.

clue.text: Deck of ship crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means going across, so the ship spans the river letter

parts.note: a pink is an old type of narrow-sterned sailing ship

explanation.surface: The deck of a ship as it crosses a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' looks like a noun, part of the ship; it is a verb meaning to adorn.
explanation.definitionFit: To prink is to dress up or adorn oneself, a synonym for deck out.

clue.text: Art able to show model's name centrally

indicators.note: centrally means in the middle, so the name letter sits in the middle of the model

parts.note: a cast is a model made in a mould

explanation.surface: Artistic skill can reveal the name of a model in the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: Art here is the archaic verb, as in 'thou art'; the 's of model's means has.
explanation.definitionFit: Canst is the old second-person form of can, so thou canst means thou art able.

clue.text: Reduce the value of record

definitions.meaning: in accounting, to lower an asset's stated value in the books
to set something on paper so it is kept

explanation.definitionFit: Write down is both an accountant's term for cutting book value and plain phrasing for putting on paper.

clue.text: Operatic heroine has to shout to make an impression

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's La Boheme
a cry is a shout

explanation.surface: An opera heroine must shout to be noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimicry is imitation, the art of doing an impression of someone.

clue.text: Aconite's habit, in part

definitions.meaning: a poisonous plant with hooded flowers, also called wolfsbane
a habit is a monk's robe, and its hood is one part of it

explanation.definitionFit: Monkshood is the common name of aconite, and a monk's hood is part of his habit.

clue.text: Deposit unexpectedly cut

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the letters turn up in a surprising new order

explanation.surface: A bank deposit is suddenly reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' reads as a verb about the deposit; it is a noun, a cut of beef.
explanation.definitionFit: Topside is a lean cut of beef from the upper hindquarter.

clue.text: Proceed instinctively during mountain climbing over a long period

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going upwards, so the mountain is read backwards

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain

indicators.note: over means covering, so the long period goes round the word for during

parts.note: a year is a long stretch of time
by can mean during, as in by night

explanation.surface: Going by instinct while climbing a mountain over many years.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbing' reads the mountain upwards, so backwards; 'over' here means covering, wrapping the long period round the small word for during.
explanation.definitionFit: To play by ear is to act without preparation, improvising according to circumstances.

clue.text: Short service soldiers overwhelmed by river suddenly

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means engulfed, so the river surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
temp is short-term work, a temporary job
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A short spell of military service ends when soldiers are suddenly swept away by a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Extempore means on the spur of the moment, without preparation, so done suddenly.

clue.text: No name with puzzle

parts.note: plus means together with

explanation.surface: A puzzle with no name attached.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to baffle or perplex them.

clue.text: Noisy party climb over archaeological site

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so the climb comes first

parts.note: to shin up is to climb using arms and legs
a dig is an archaeological excavation

explanation.surface: A loud party that climbs over an excavation.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is a lively, noisy party or celebration.

clue.text: Fixed rented accommodation

parts.note: a flat rate is a fixed one
let means rented out

explanation.surface: Rented accommodation at a fixed price.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatlet is a small flat, a compact apartment to live in.

clue.text: Renamed island is an outline with nothing on it

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the nothing comes before it

parts.note: a form is a shape or outline
O looks like zero, nothing
it is sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: An island with a new name has an empty outline on the map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' meaning sex appeal (SA) is old slang from the film It.
explanation.definitionFit: Formosa is the former Portuguese-derived name of Taiwan, renamed since.

clue.text: Level ground

definitions.meaning: a sports field, as a cricket or football field

explanation.definitionFit: Pitch means a degree or height of intensity, and also a playing field.

clue.text: 'Over and out' — that's 'Roger' 's announcement primarily

parts.note: ex means out of or former

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so the opening letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A radio operator signs off, and that is the gist of the announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over and out' and 'Roger' are radio sign-offs; 'Over' is the definition, meaning spare or additional.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means more than is needed, surplus, left over.

clue.text: Flourish, making money during a period of growth

parts.note: a boom is a period of rapid economic growth

explanation.surface: Thriving by earning money in an economic boom.
explanation.definitionFit: To bloom is to flourish or be in one's prime.

clue.text: Bulb lit? One lit

parts.note: a light that is lit is on
I is the Roman numeral for one
again, lit means on

explanation.surface: Is the bulb lit? One is lit.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion is a vegetable bulb.

clue.text: Fish that rise occasionally use their heads

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters, so each word's opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Fish that rise to the surface now and then use their heads.
explanation.definitionFit: A trout is a freshwater game fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Just after St Andrew's day enters cathedral to get a book

indicators.note: enters means goes inside, so the date sits within the cathedral

parts.note: duomo is Italian for cathedral
St Andrew's day is 30 November, so the day after is 1 December, Dec I

explanation.surface: Just after Scotland's patron saint's day, someone walks into a cathedral to collect a book.
explanation.walkthrough: St Andrew is Scotland's patron saint; his day is 30 November.
explanation.definitionFit: A duodecimo is a book of small page size, each sheet folded into twelve leaves.

clue.text: Conceal park official, so to speak, in shrub…

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the words are heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: conceal is hide, a park official is a ranger

explanation.surface: A park warden is hidden in a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydrangea is a flowering shrub with large heads of blooms.

clue.text: …in which sweep is concealed

indicators.note: is concealed means sits hidden inside, so only the inner stretch of the previous answer is kept

parts.note: which refers back to the shrub of the clue before

explanation.surface: Continuing the shrub, which hides a sweep.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 27 Across: the answer sits within the shrub's name, which also hid the ranger.
explanation.definitionFit: Range means scope or extent, the sweep of something.
